newsitem.title: UK: Oil market on Iraq alert, dollar slips from peaks.
newsitem.headline: Oil market on Iraq alert, dollar slips from peaks.

text.p: World energy markets were on alert on Thursday after tension over Iraq propelled the price of oil to a post-Gulf war high and the dollar retreated from near two-month peaks against the mark and yen scaled in Europe the previous day.

On the bourses, leading shares in London and Paris traded significantly higher after a positive overnight close on Wall Street, which ended nearly half a percent up. Frankfurt, however, was less bullish but still in positive territory, marking time ahead of key U.S. producer prices due out later in the day.
Another round of U.S.-Iraq tensions put crude oil markets on full alert as Washington signalled it would retaliate for an Iraqi missile attack on U.S. warplanes.

News that Iraq had launched the surface-to-air missile at two U.S. fighters propelled energy prices. Benchmark Brent crude rose overnight in Asia to a peak of $23.80 per barrel, its highest since Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990 and pushed Brent prices to $40.95.

On the foreign exchange front, the dollar drifted lower in the European morning, unable to sustain Wednesday's rally to 1.5155 marks and 110.40 yen as short-term players took profits above 110 yen and 1.51 marks, dealers said.

"People have become a bit wary after the dollar failed to hold above 110 yen and 1.51 marks," said Chris Tinker, chief economist at Standard Chartered. "The range-trading mentality has returned to the market, with a bias to test the downside."

A near-term rise in U.S.interest rates was priced into the dollar, analysts said and signs of strength in the August U.S. producer price data (due at 1230 GMT), and Friday's consumer prices, would cement the outlook for a credit tightening.
The inflation data moved into focus after comments from Federal Reserve Governor Janet Yellen on Tuesday, who said the U.S. economy had entered an inflationary danger zone.
On European bourses, leading London shares were steady around the day's best level late morning after absorbing a stream of largely upbeat company and inflation news.
Results from over 40 companies, including seven from the blue chip FTSE 100 index, contained few unpleasant surprises but gains were held back by continuing caution ahead of the U.S. economic data.

Broadly in-line British retail price data had little effect on the market and by 1045 GMT, the FTSE 100 had edged up to 3,924.7, a rise of 19.1 points on the day and just 8.9 points off its all-time high set on September 10.
The Paris bourse also advanced, led by French banking stocks which opened higher on the back of rising bond prices. By 1045 the CAC-40 index was up three quarters of a percent.
In Frankfurt leading German stocks were less bullish with dealers saying uncertainty about interest rates and the forthcoming U.S. data was holding things back.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5105 marks and 109.90 yen compared with late Wednesday's 1.5079 marks and 110.20 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 19.1 points up at 3,924.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 15.69 points up at 2,053.75.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was 2.57 points up at 2,569.37.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $382.20 compared with its London close on Wednesday of 383.65. Silver was down two cents at $5.08.
